question: Identify all paths up to three hops long connecting an account with account_id 'ACC000000' to any other node.
sql: SELECT graph.n1, graph.n2 FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('financial_fraud_detection', 'MATCH (n1:ACCOUNT)-[e]-{1,3}(n2) WHERE n1.account_id = ''ACC000000'' RETURN n1, n2 LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(n1 VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', n2 VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('financial_fraud_detection', 'MATCH (n1:ACCOUNT)-[e]-{1,3}(n2) WHERE n1.account_id = ''ACC000000'' RETURN n1, n2 LIMIT 5')
reason: This query triggers an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) error because Leapfrog Triejoin (try_ltj) does not support variable-length repeating patterns (-{1,3}) in large datasets. As a result, the engine falls back to general match pattern execution, which evaluates the relationship repetition globally across the entire 57MB database first. In a highly connected transaction graph, the number of paths of length 3 grows exponentially to tens of millions or billions, exhausting system memory and causing the OS OOM killer to terminate the mysqld process.
